content: Deaths that occur during pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period (puerperium) are classified as direct maternal deaths if they result from complications of pregnancy, labor, or delivery. Currently, these underlying causes of death do not have an O code in the ICD-10 classification system. It is recommended that certifiers explicitly indicate the pregnancy status on death certificates to reduce underreporting of suicides during pregnancy. When certain conditions complicate pregnancy, are worsened by pregnancy, or necessitate obstetric care, an additional code from Chapter I of the ICD-10 may be used to specify the condition if desired. For example, unspecified maternal infectious or parasitic diseases complicating pregnancy, childbirth, or the puerperium must include the code O98 (Maternal infectious and parasitic diseases classifiable elsewhere but complicating pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium). The WHO's application of ICD-10 to deaths during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium (ICD-MM) provides specific codes for maternal diseases that complicate pregnancy. These include conditions aggravated by pregnancy or those requiring obstetric care, even if the Alphabetical Index does not specify a particular rubric. Additional codes may be used to identify specific conditions if desired. Indirect maternal deaths, which result from pre-existing medical conditions or diseases aggravated by pregnancy, may also be coded using ICD codes from other chapters. Accurate reporting on death certificates is essential, particularly in Part 1, to indicate any mutual aggravation between the condition and pregnancy. Rare diseases are categorized under Other – specify, and most medical and surgical conditions have corresponding ICD codes. Examples of indirect causes of maternal death include diseases of the nervous system (e.g., epilepsy, G40), circulatory system (e.g., rheumatic heart disease, I09; cardiomyopathy, I42), respiratory system (e.g., asthma, J45), digestive system (e.g., pancreatitis, K85), musculoskeletal system (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, M32), and genitourinary system (e.g., renal conditions). Exclusions apply to conditions like liver disease and cerebral hemorrhage due to pre-eclampsia. Maternal deaths from unspecified causes during pregnancy, labor, delivery, or the puerperium are categorized under Group 9: Coincidental causes. These deaths occur during pregnancy or the postpartum period but are not classified as maternal deaths by definition. Examples include motor vehicle accidents (ICD codes Y85, V01–V99), external causes of accidental injury (W00–Y04, Y06–Y09), assault (X85–Y04, Y06–Y09), and events of undetermined intent (Y10–Y34). The WHO's ICD-MM Annex B2 provides a tabular list of Chapter 15 codes describing conditions unlikely to cause death but potentially contributing to it. Codes from Annex B1 are preferred, and those from Annex B2 should not be selected as the underlying cause of death if a condition from Annex B1 is present. If the cause of death is unspecified, it should be coded as Unknown, Group 8 according to MRG 1244. Identifying maternal deaths can be challenging, particularly in cases of indirect obstetric causes. If there is doubt about whether the cause of death is obstetric, additional information should be sought from the certifier. This is especially important in countries with high maternal mortality rates. If no further information is available, deaths mentioning pregnancy or delivery in Part 1 of the death certificate should be considered obstetric, but not if mentioned only in Part 2. Further modifications in the 11th revision of the ICD may result in changes to these classifications. For example, complications following abortion, ectopic pregnancy, or molar pregnancy are coded under O08, primarily for morbidity coding. Additional codes may be used to identify specific complications, such as septic shock. Other conditions, such as vomiting complicating pregnancy, delayed delivery of multiple fetuses, or prolonged labor, are contributory conditions and do not provide sufficient detail on the cause of death alone. Codes O64–O66 are tabulated under other obstetric causes and considered direct maternal deaths when indicated as the cause of death. The mode of delivery (e.g., undelivered, normal vaginal, assisted vaginal, cesarean section, abortion/miscarriage) and pregnancy outcome (e.g., miscarriage/abortion, antenatal death, intrapartum death, neonatal death, alive) should also be documented for any maternal death. Countries may include a checklist of contributory conditions (e.g., HIV infection, anemia, previous cesarean section, prolonged labor, female genital mutilation, obesity, depression, domestic violence) on maternal death data sheets to facilitate data collection and analysis.
